claims.head: Special teams lean toward the Red Wings
claims.call: The Red Wings’ power play creates at least their usual 8.5 expected goals per 60.
claims.body: The Red Wings’ power play is one of the league’s best, and the Sharks’ kill is near the bottom of the league. Every trip to the box hurts the Sharks more than most.
claims.nums: Detroit 4th for power play (8.5 expected goals per 60) · San Jose 26th for penalty kill
claims.gist: The Red Wings’ power play has a soft target in the Sharks’ kill.

check.measure: expected goals per 60 on the power play
check.rule: held if tonight's figure is at or above the team's usual level; partly if between the league average and that level; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: The Red Wings should pile up the shots
claims.call: The Red Wings take at least their usual 60.7 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5.
claims.body: The Red Wings shoot a lot, and the Sharks are around the middle of the league at keeping shots down. Look for a big shot total.

claims.gist: The Red Wings shoot a lot, and the Sharks give up plenty.

claims.body: The Sharks and the Red Wings are both among the league’s heaviest hitters, even after adjusting for each arena’s scorer. Keep your head up.

notes.text: M. Celebrini returned in their last game after missing 2 games.
M. Kasper is out week to week and has missed the last 3 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
J. Compher is on injured reserve and has missed the last 2 games.
S. Edvinsson has not played this season. He is a top-pair defenseman. A. Johansson has taken his spot beside M. Seider.

DET.head: Detroit should have the upper hand
DET.body: Detroit has had more of the chances over recent games, Detroit will be without Kasper, and Detroit has home ice. San Jose can make it interesting if they pounce on loose pucks.

SJS.head: A tough matchup for San Jose
SJS.body: Detroit has had more of the chances over recent games, Detroit will be without Kasper, and Detroit has home ice. San Jose’s best way through is pouncing on loose pucks.
